# Results — Study 111 (VIX-Term-Structure) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The VIX term-structure
slope (log(^VIX3M / ^VIX)) is tested as a predictor of SPY forward returns and as a
binary timing overlay.  Contango (slope > 0, VIX < VIX3M) is the claimed 'risk-on'
state; backwardation (slope < 0) is the claimed stress signal.  Real daily tape: ^VIX,
^VIX3M, SPY from 2008-01-03 (^VIX3M launch) through 2026-06-12.  As-of **2026-06-13**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | N days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| ^VIX, ^VIX3M, SPY | 2008-01-03 → 2026-06-12 | 4 640 | `e78f42c8162e` |

Fraction of days in contango (slope > 0): **89.7%** — the term structure spends the
vast majority of time in contango, with backwardation concentrated in crisis episodes
(2008–09, 2011, 2020, 2022).

## The central test — Q5-Q1 quintile spread

Slope is sorted into rolling quintiles (252-day lookback, out-of-sample); forward SPY
log-returns are computed for each bucket; the Q5 (steepest contango) minus Q1 (deepest
backwardation) spread is the decisive test of the claim.

| Horizon | n Q5 | n Q1 | mean Q5 (bps) | mean Q1 (bps) | spread (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 day** | 1 148 | 931 | **+2.25** | **+3.23** | **−0.98** | **−0.08** |
| **5 days** | 1 148 | 929 | +11.75 | +23.36 | −11.61 | −0.36 |
| **21 days** | 1 140 | 928 | +80.37 | +127.63 | −47.25 | −0.47 |

The Q5-Q1 spread is **negative at all horizons** — the opposite of the claim.
Backwardation episodes (Q1, stress, VIX spike) are followed by *better* average SPY
returns than the calmest contango days (Q5).  Every HAC t-stat is far inside ±2 and
points in the wrong direction.

### Full quintile forward-return table (h = 1 day)

| Quintile | Regime | n | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 | Deepest backwardation | 931 | +3.23 | +0.61 |
| Q2 | Mild backwardation | 786 | +5.12 | +1.20 |
| Q3 | Near-flat / transition | 831 | +9.76 | +2.91 |
| Q4 | Moderate contango | 881 | +2.81 | +1.01 |
| Q5 | Steepest contango | 1 148 | +2.25 | +1.08 |

There is no monotone ascent from Q1 to Q5; the pattern is non-monotone and Q3 (the
transition zone near flat) shows the highest mean — likely a sample artefact given
~35 years of equity drift.

## Binary timing overlay — long in contango, flat in backwardation

The 'risk-on' rule: be long SPY when yesterday's slope was positive, else hold cash.

| Arm | mean (bps/day) | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Timing overlay (active)** | **+3.20** | **+0.57** | **+2.50** |
| **Buy-and-hold (passive)** | **+4.25** | **+0.54** | **+2.64** |
| **Spread (active − passive)** | **−1.05** | — | **−1.01** |

The timer *underperforms* buy-and-hold by **1.05 bps/day** (~−2.6%/yr) at zero cost.
The spread t-stat is −1.01 — not statistically significant, but consistently on the
wrong side.  Because the market is in backwardation only ~10% of the time, the timer
misses those days entirely and sits in cash during some of the highest-returning crisis
reversals.

### Cost sweep (spread = active − passive)

~14 switches per year (contango↔backwardation transitions).

| Round-trip cost | Spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps | −1.05 | −1.01 |
| 0.5 bps | −1.07 | −1.04 |
| 1.0 bps | −1.10 | −1.06 |
| 2.0 bps | −1.16 | −1.12 |
| 5.0 bps | −1.33 | −1.28 |

The spread starts negative and only deteriorates with costs — **there is no positive
break-even cost**.

## Regime comparison

| Regime | n | % of tape | mean (bps/day) | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Full sample | 4 638 | 100% | +4.30 | +0.55 | +2.68 |
| **Contango (slope > 0)** | 4 159 | 89.7% | **+3.57** | **+0.60** | **+2.51** |
| **Backwardation (slope < 0)** | 479 | 10.3% | **+10.64** | **+0.62** | **+1.04** |

Backwardation episodes deliver **nearly 3x** the contango daily return (+10.6 vs +3.6
bps/day).  The difference is not statistically significant (the backwardation sample is
only 479 days), but it is directionally the **opposite** of the claimed effect — the
'stress' regime is followed by higher returns, not lower.  This is consistent with a
**volatility risk premium** / crisis-rebound story: markets recover more strongly after
the very episodes the slope flags as dangerous.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Q5-Q1 spread is −0.98 bps (wrong sign) with HAC *t* = −0.08
  at h = 1d.  No horizon produces a t-stat above 0.5 or a spread in the predicted
  (positive) direction.  The VIX/VIX3M slope does not predict SPY forward returns.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The timing overlay trails buy-and-hold by ~2.6%/yr at zero
  cost; every bp of switching cost widens the gap.  Trend t-stat = −1.01 on the spread.
- **Beats buy-and-hold? — NO.** The timer misses the strongest post-crisis rebounds
  (which occur in backwardation) and underperforms unconditional equity exposure.
